markdown.srcMarkdownNoYaml:
## Recap - You've looked at measurements. - You've implemented some code to process a measurement (create a vector representation) - You've looked at pairs of measurements. - You've implemented code to compare measurements (compute vector similarity and distance) - You've looked at collections of measurements. - You've conducted a library search, and we've discussed clustering and dimensionality reduction techniques that can be used with collections of vectors ## What is a sample? :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"}
A **sample** is a physical material we are trying to identify (or classify or safely dispose of or otherwise deal with) - [Usually a subset of a larger population]{style="font-size:85%"} - [Insights from the sample may allow us to infer something about the population]{style="font-size:85%"} ::: ::: {.column width="40%"} ![](../figures/White-Powder.png){fig-align="center"} ::: :::: ## What is a structure? :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"}
A **structure** is a human-defined representation of the relationship between the atoms that constitute a compound - [Names [**common** vs IUPAC]]{style="font-size:65%"} - [Encodings [**SMILES** vs InChI vs InChIKey]]{style="font-size:65%"} - [Diagrams [Line drawings]]{style="font-size:65%"} [How materials are described; How materials are scheduled]{.fragment} ::: ::: {.column width="40%"} ![](../figures/Caffeine_structure.svg){fig-align="center"} ::: :::: ## Are these three structures similar? :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="33%"} ![](../figures/heroin.svg){width=100%} ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} ![](../figures/fentanyl.svg){width=100%} ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} ![](../figures/d9-thc.svg){width=100%} ::: :::: ## How can we objectively compare structures? - If we create vector representations of information contained in the structure, we can use the same math tools we used with vectors of measurements!

- $\mathrm{Heroin}\rightarrow\mathrm{C}_{21}\mathrm{H}_{23}\mathrm{N}\mathrm{O}_{5} \rightarrow [21,23,1,5]$ - $\mathrm{Fentanyl}\rightarrow \mathrm{C}_{22}\mathrm{H}_{26}\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O} \rightarrow [n_C,n_H,n_N,n_O]$ - $\Delta 9 \mathrm{THC}\rightarrow\mathrm{C}_{21}\mathrm{H}_{30}\mathrm{O}_{2} \rightarrow [n_C,n_H,n_N,n_O]$

- *Molecular fingerprints* are vector encodings that account for various structural (and other) information that can be pulled form a compound ## Working with chemical structures - the ```rcdk``` package is an R interface to a very popular cheminformatics library (Chemistry Development Kit) - ```rdkit``` is a python interface to the same library ::: {.fragment} ```{r} #| eval: FALSE if("rcdk" %in% installed.packages()==FALSE) install.packages("rcdk") library(rcdk) Library = readRDS("asm_ReferenceMSLibrary_SWDRUG314.RDS") # loads the reference library heroin = 1836 # these are the index values in our RDS library fentanyl = 1906 # these are the index values in our RDS library d9THC = 3284 # these are the index values in our RDS library ``` ::: ## Extracting the SMILES from the library - Step 1: We want to pull the [SMILES](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simplified_Molecular_Input_Line_Entry_System){target="_blank"} for the compounds ::: {.fragment} ```{r} #| eval: FALSE heroin_SMILES_messedUp = Library$IndexData$SMILES[heroin] heroin_SMILES = strsplit(heroin_SMILES_messedUp,"\t")[[1]][1] heroin_mol = parse.smiles(heroin_SMILES)[[1]] # function from rcdk package # view.molecule.2d(heroin_mol) # function from the rcdk package ``` ::: - We'll streamline the process for the other two compounds ::: {.fragment} ```{r} #| eval: FALSE fentanyl_SMILES = strsplit(Library$IndexData$SMILES[fentanyl],"\t")[[1]][1] fentanyl_mol = parse.smiles(fentanyl_SMILES)[[1]] d9THC_SMILES = strsplit(Library$IndexData$SMILES[d9THC],"\t")[[1]][1] d9THC_mol = parse.smiles(d9THC_SMILES)[[1]] ``` ::: ## Converting SMILES to fingerprint - Step 2. We want to convert the SMILES to a molecular fingerprint ::: {.fragment} ```{r} #| eval: FALSE heroin_fp = get.fingerprint(heroin_mol,type="standard") # function from the rcdk package fentanyl_fp = get.fingerprint(fentanyl_mol,type="standard") d9THC_fp = get.fingerprint(d9THC_mol,type="standard") ``` ::: - Step 3. "Extract" the vector from the molecular fingerprint information ::: {.fragment} ```{r} #| eval: FALSE heroin_x = numeric(heroin_fp@nbit) heroin_x[heroin_fp@bits] = 1 fentanyl_x = numeric(fentanyl_fp@nbit) fentanyl_x[fentanyl_fp@bits] = 1 d9THC_x = numeric(d9THC_fp@nbit) d9THC_x[d9THC_fp@bits] = 1 ``` ::: ## Numerical comparison of molecular fingerprints - We can use the same machinery that we developed for comparing mass spectra to compare fingerprints ::: {.fragment} ```{r} #| eval: FALSE source("CustomFunctions/LibrarySearchFunctions.R") cat(paste0("Similarity between heroin and fentanyl: ", euclideanDistance(heroin_x,fentanyl_x),"\n")) cat(paste0("Similarity between heroin and d9-THC: ",euclideanDistance(heroin_x,d9THC_x),"\n")) cat(paste0("Similarity between d9THC and fentanyl: ",euclideanDistance(d9THC_x,fentanyl_x),"\n")) ``` ::: - **NOTE:** most people wouldn't use a euclidean distance to compare "barcode" data like fingerprints, they would use a *Tanimoto index* or other measure of overlap ## Visual comparison of molecular fingerprints - We can use the same machinery that we developed for comparing mass spectra to compare fingerprints with some minor modifications ::: {.fragment} ```{r} #| eval: false HT_plot(seq(heroin_fp@nbit),heroin_x,seq(fentanyl_fp@nbit),fentanyl_x) HT_plot(seq(heroin_fp@nbit),heroin_x,seq(d9THC_fp@nbit),d9THC_x) HT_plot(seq(d9THC_fp@nbit),d9THC_x,seq(fentanyl_fp@nbit),fentanyl_x) ``` ::: ## Key Points - Chemometrics/informatics are very similar - The first step is the hardest: coming up with a reasonable way to represent the information as a vector - some articles call this encoding, embedding, feature selection - most articles do not explain how they do this - The second step is implementing numerical algorithms to work with vectors - not as hard anymore with open source packages - Decisions at each step will affect results and interpretations, important to be explicit about design choices ## Chemical Space! - Let's create plots representing "chemical space" by looking at the structural and spectral similarity of all unique combinations of a set of compounds ::: {.fragment} ```{r} #| eval: false rm(list=ls()) source("CustomFunctions/LibrarySearchFunctions.R") Library = readRDS("asm_ReferenceMSLibrary_SWDRUG314.RDS") if("rcdk" %in% installed.packages()==FALSE) install.packages("rcdk") library(rcdk) nCompounds = 50 COI = sample(seq(1,dim(Library$IndexData)[1]),nCompounds) # selecting a random set of compounds of interest (COI) nComputes = (nCompounds^2-nCompounds)/2 SpecSimScores = numeric(nComputes) StrucSimScores = numeric(nComputes) labels = character(nComputes) counter = 0 stime <- system.time({ for(i in 1:nCompounds){ SMILES_i = strsplit(Library$IndexData$SMILES[COI[i]],"\t")[[1]][1] mol_i = parse.smiles(SMILES_i)[[1]] fp_i = get.fingerprint(mol_i,type="standard")@bits # pulling the bits directly indices_i = which(Library$SpectralData$SpecID==COI[i]) spec_mz_i = Library$SpectralData$mz[indices_i] spec_int = Library$SpectralData$int[indices_i] spec_int_i = spec_int/max(spec_int) for(j in 1:nCompounds){ if(i >= j) next SMILES_j = strsplit(Library$IndexData$SMILES[COI[j]],"\t")[[1]][1] mol_j = parse.smiles(SMILES_j)[[1]] fp_j = get.fingerprint(mol_j,type="standard")@bits indices_j = which(Library$SpectralData$SpecID==COI[j]) spec_mz_j = Library$SpectralData$mz[indices_j] spec_int = Library$SpectralData$int[indices_j] spec_int_j = spec_int/max(spec_int) maxmz = max(spec_mz_i,spec_mz_j) A = spec2vec(spec_mz_i,spec_int_i,maxmz) B = spec2vec(spec_mz_j,spec_int_j,maxmz) counter = counter + 1 SpecSimScores[counter] = cosineSim(A,B) StrucSimScores[counter] = length(intersect(fp_i,fp_j))/length(union(fp_i,fp_j)) # this is a Tanimoto similarity coefficient labels[counter] = paste0(Library$IndexData$Name[COI[i]],"\n vs. \n", Library$IndexData$Name[COI[j]]) } } })[3] cat(paste0("This computation took ",round(stime,3)," seconds.\n")) plot(SpecSimScores,StrucSimScores) text(SpecSimScores,StrucSimScores,labels,cex=0.5) ``` ::: ##
